1. Purchase Price. Buyer cannot agree to USD 45,000,000. Based on the information currently available and Buyer’s preliminary valuation work, Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 38,000,000.

2. Closing. The proposed 30-day closing period is too compressed. Buyer requires sufficient time for confirmatory diligence, financing/approval processes, and review of closing deliverables and consents. Please revise Section 2 to provide that closing will occur no earlier than 45 days after signing and only following satisfaction or waiver of all conditions, including receipt of all required third-party and regulatory consents and completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence.

3. Financial Statement Representation. Buyer is not prepared to accept the financial statement representation solely on a knowledge-qualified basis. Please remove “to the Seller’s knowledge.” The representation should state that the financial statements fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, subject only to normal year-end adjustments. In addition, the reference to “notes and assumptions reflected therein” should be deleted unless those notes and assumptions are specifically identified and delivered to Buyer.

4. Additional Buyer Protections. Buyer expects the agreement to include customary interim operating covenants, access rights, indemnification provisions, bring-down conditions, and termination rights. We can provide markup language in the next draft.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting the above.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable following signing and in any event no later than 40 days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, receipt of required third-party and regulatory consents, and delivery of customary closing deliverables. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete its confirmatory diligence and financing or approval processes within such period, and confirmatory diligence shall not constitute a separate condition to Closing except to the extent expressly set forth in this Agreement.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the notes and assumptions specifically reflected in such financial statements or otherwise delivered to Buyer in writing prior to signing.

5. Interim Operating Covenants. From signing until Closing, except as otherwise contemplated by this Agreement, required by applicable law, or consented to by Buyer in writing, the Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and not take any action outside the ordinary course that would materially impair the value of the Shares or the Company, provided that Buyer’s consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

6. Access. From signing until Closing, Seller shall provide Buyer and its representatives reasonable access, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, to the Company’s books, records, personnel, and facilities for confirmatory diligence purposes, provided that such access shall not unreasonably interfere with the Company’s business and shall remain subject to applicable law, confidentiality obligations, and reasonable privilege protections.

7. Indemnification. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from any breach of Seller’s representations, warranties, and covenants contained in this Agreement, subject to customary limitations, including survival periods, a deductible or basket, a cap, mitigation requirements, and exclusions for punitive, special, consequential, or multiple-based damages except to the extent awarded to a third party.

8. Bring-Down Condition. Buyer’s obligation to close shall be conditioned on Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct at Closing, except for failures to be true and correct that would not reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect, and Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing.

9. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated by mutual written consent, by either party if Closing has not occurred within 40 days after signing other than as a result of such party’s material breach, by either party upon a final non-appealable legal restraint prohibiting the transaction, or by the non-breaching party upon an uncured material breach by the other party following reasonable written notice and an opportunity to cure.

receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the addition of a framework for interim covenants, access, indemnity, bring-down, and termination. Subject to final documentation, Buyer is prepared to move forward on the following basis.

First, price remains above Buyer’s view of value given the remaining confirmatory work and the current allocation of risk. Buyer can proceed at USD 39,000,000.

Second, the 40-day closing period is still too compressed for third-party/regulatory consents, confirmatory review, and internal approvals. Please revise the outside date to 60 days after signing. Buyer will use commercially reasonable efforts, but Buyer should not be deemed in breach where delays result from third-party/regulatory timing or Seller/Company delays in providing information or access.

Third, confirmatory diligence cannot be purely aspirational. Buyer’s closing obligation should be conditioned on completion of confirmatory diligence without discovery of any matter that would reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, the Shares, or Buyer’s valuation. Buyer also requires express conditions for required consents, no material adverse effect, accuracy of Seller’s representations at closing, and Seller’s covenant compliance.

Fourth, the financial statement representation should read that the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, subject only to normal year-end adjustments and the notes expressly set forth in such financial statements. Please delete the broader reference to assumptions or other materials delivered separately prior to signing.

Fifth, the provisions currently shown as tracked additions for interim operating covenants, access, indemnification, bring-down, and termination should be integrated into the operative text of the agreement. We can work from Seller’s framework, but the indemnity needs definitive terms: general reps to survive 18 months; fundamental reps to survive 6 years; no basket for fraud or fundamental reps; a customary basket for general reps; a cap of at least 15% of the purchase price for general reps; and fundamental reps capped at the purchase price.

Finally, please revise confidentiality to permit disclosure to Buyer’s affiliates, representatives, financing sources, insurers, regulators, and as required by law, subject to customary confidentiality protections where applicable.

If Seller can accept the above, Buyer is prepared to turn a clean execution draft promptly.
